projects.title: Social Sentiment Analysis
projects.description: Evaluate three-class sentiment against human labels, inspect confusion patterns, and compare the selected model with a transparent baseline.
projects.change: The evaluation includes independent calibration, uncertainty intervals, development-only stability checks and an auditable error analysis. A reproducible results gallery presents the evidence visually.
projects.limitation: Historical social posts; no measurement of Black Friday public opinion or current customer sentiment. A separately labelled, representative sample from the intended customer channel would be needed to validate a feedback workflow.

images.alt: Social Sentiment Analysis — benchmark results overview
images.caption: Published project summary · historical benchmark
The confusion matrix includes all 12,284 official test posts. Model selection uses validation; a higher-scoring test candidate does not replace the selected model.
Recall and support are measured against the human-labelled official test set. Intervals describe benchmark uncertainty, not future customer channels.
Candidates are shown for inspection. The selected TF-IDF model remains fixed from validation macro F1 even if another candidate has a higher test score.

images.alt: Score reliability and support by probability band
images.caption: Published phase-two output · benchmark probabilities

projects.title: Click Propensity & Ranking
projects.eyebrow: Put attention where the signal is
projects.description: Explore how a ranking model concentrates observed click labels, with probability calibration and the sampling limits kept in view.
projects.change: The evaluation includes independent calibration, uncertainty intervals, development-only stability checks and an auditable error analysis. A reproducible results gallery presents the evidence visually.
projects.limitation: The benchmark has downsampled negatives and no representative campaign timelines or population click rate. Representative impression logs, timestamps and an independent campaign evaluation would be needed before interpreting scores as real campaign probabilities.

images.alt: Click Propensity & Ranking — benchmark results overview
images.caption: Published project summary · historical benchmark
The gains curve describes the sampled test set. The top-10% point has 799 contexts and captures 269 click labels; it is not a population CTR estimate.
Model and prior-baseline losses are measured on the same group-isolated test partition. Lower log loss is better; this does not restore population prevalence.
Position groups describe test-set error patterns. Moving an ad to another position is a hypothetical model change, not a measured causal effect.

images.alt: Score reliability and support by probability band
images.caption: Published phase-two output · benchmark probabilities
